QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_44

question.text: 'Tapti Growth Category II AIF' is negotiating a term sheet for a INR 50 crore investment at 15% equity. The founders are cash-strapped and push back on 2x participating liquidation preference. Mr. Shankar Rao, fund manager, wants downside protection WITHOUT penalising the founders on a strong exit. The BEST middle-ground structure is:

answer.text: Agree to 1x non-participating preference — gives INR 50 cr floor; if exit is rich, AIF converts and takes 15% pro-rata

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes liquidation preference as downside protection equal to the investment or a multiple thereof, and distinguishes non-participating preference (investor takes the preferred amount OR converts and takes the pro-rata equity share) from participating "double-dip" economics. The 1x non-participating structure returns capital on a weak exit and lets the AIF convert and take its 15% pro-rata share on a rich exit, without double-dipping. The Trap: 3x and 5x participating sit at the punitive end of the spectrum and are inconsistent with the "middle-ground" brief. Dropping all liquidation preference removes the downside protection the workbook frames as the core purpose of the clause. Note: The mechanics for non-participating versus participating preference appear on pages 229-230; the workbook does not quote market-share statistics for the structure or a specific exit-multiple cut-off.
